llm.summary: This browser automation skill is disclosed, but it exposes a persistent local control service that can run arbitrary browser and Node-side code without meaningful guardrails.

dimensions.detail: The daemon listens on 127.0.0.1:19223 and accepts unauthenticated HTTP GET commands, including arbitrary code execution, while retaining the browser session across commands.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a normal npm/Playwright setup, but package.json uses an unpinned caret dependency and no lockfile, so installs are not reproducible.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions include powerful examples for localStorage access, downloads, form submission, and rich-text overwrite/save flows without requiring explicit user confirmation or a read-only default.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill starts a long-running browser daemon, stores daemon state under ~/.pw-browser, can write screenshots/downloads, and can mutate authenticated web pages through the active browser session.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Most capabilities fit browser automation, and eval/run-code are documented, but run-code is implemented with new Function against the live Playwright page and can execute arbitrary Node-side code from the daemon context.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the skill control of a local browser session and arbitrary code execution authority. Use it on logged-in or sensitive sites only with clear user intent, prefer the structured commands over run-code/eval, close the daemon after use, and review or pin the Playwright dependency before operational use.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The daemon, eval, and run-code capabilities are disclosed in the artifact, so the framing is not hidden; the remaining concern is that the disclosed authority is very broad.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The arbitrary execution surface is confirmed in pw-browser.js and is broader than bounded click/fill/screenshot automation.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The eval and run-code paths execute caller-supplied code against the active page and daemon context without authentication, allowlisting, or confirmation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The safety-warning concern is supported: examples cover storage reads, downloads, form submission, and publish/save actions without explicit safeguards.
[SC1] unexpected: The Playwright dependency is purpose-aligned, but the caret range and missing lockfile make the install non-deterministic.
[SC4] unexpected: The artifact does not lock exactly playwright 1.51.0, so the exact-version claim is not fully artifact-backed; however the declared lower bound is old and dependency review is warranted.
